blocks.text: An S3 object contains data and metadata; its key identifies it within a bucket. Upload with aws s3 cp from local file to bucket/key; download reverses the endpoints. Keep profile and Region explicit. Buckets are created in an AWS Region; verify location and caller access.

steps.title: Verify the intended object and context

blocks.text: The upload goes from orders-release.zip to s3://orders-sandbox-artifacts-lab/releases/orders-release.zip. The download reads that same bucket/key into retrieved/orders-release.zip. The key releases/orders-release.zip identifies the object within orders-sandbox-artifacts-lab; a familiar local filename or key alone does not establish the intended storage location.

Both commands use profile orders-sandbox-operator and verified bucket Region us-east-1. The supplied access evidence says: Caller can upload and retrieve the intended bucket/key. After retrieval, the supplied comparison says: Retrieved artifact matches the supplied orders-release.zip file. A file arriving locally is not enough if its bucket/key differs from the intended object. Check endpoints, location and access rather than inferring them from the filename.

In the same transfer evidence, upload has local source orders-release.zip and S3 destination s3://orders-sandbox-artifacts-lab/releases/orders-release.zip; download reverses the direction into a local destination. Use aws s3 cp with explicit profile orders-sandbox-operator and Region us-east-1 in both directions. A bucket is created in a Region: verify its intended location and caller access, rather than assuming them from the filename.

An S3 object consists of data and metadata. In the same evidence, releases/orders-release.zip is the key within bucket orders-sandbox-artifacts-lab; orders-release.zip is the local upload source. Those are different roles. With aws s3 cp, upload goes local → S3 bucket/key and download goes from that same S3 bucket/key → local, keeping explicit profile and Region. A familiar local filename is not a substitute for verifying the intended bucket/key.
